newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch ATA says no plans to ditch wheat futures.
newsitem.headline: Dutch ATA says no plans to ditch wheat futures.

text.p: Amsterdam's Agricultural Futures exchange (ATA) said on Wednesday it had no plans to close down its fledgling wheat futures contract despite very low interest.
"There is no question of that, it's not on the agenda," ATA spokesman Kasper Walet told Reuters.
The bourse said early last month it was reviewing the contract, launched in the summer, fuelling market speculation that the ATA would withdraw it altogether.
"We're still reviewing what changes need to be made, if any," Walet added. "There is a big meeting of traders in Antwerp later this week and we will be talking to people there."

The ATA has said the timing of the launch, in between harvests, was to blame for lacklustre participation and that it was conducting an informal "sounding out" process with potential users. There are no plans to publish the results of the review.

This summer the ATA and France's MATIF entered into a race to set up a Europe-wide contract for the continent's farmers producing bread milling wheat. The Dutch exchange won with its June launch and the MATIF contract, which has also been plagued by disappointing turnover, was launched around a month later.
